key.explanation: All-time downloads can only rise and may sit several unvalidated hops from revenue, retention, or margin. It is true but not decision-useful.
CAC = acquisition cost ÷ acquired customers = ₹3,00,000 ÷ 120 = ₹2,500.
Lean validation tests whether demand is actually present before costly building or campaigning. The test and its decision threshold matter more than collecting agreeable opinions.
Lifecycle engagement supports the loop by helping users at the relevant moment. A generic drip is activity without state logic.
Profile completion may correlate because only motivated survivors finish it. The team must locate the actual value event and reduce friction before it.
Pricing architecture determines how customers enter, use, upgrade, and expand—not only what one transaction costs.
Respondents may be sincere and still mispredict their future behaviour. Surveys are useful tools, but hypothetical willingness is weak purchase evidence.
Marketing brings and shapes demand; product creates/delivers value; growth joins the transitions and measures the system.
A stage should represent a real change in buyer commitment or qualification. Otherwise pipeline math cannot locate the constraint.
Aggregate totals can rise while every cohort becomes less healthy. Cohorts hold entry time constant and expose the leak.
A loop is self-feeding by design. A spike can be large and still end when the campaign ends.
The null is the default no-effect or no-difference position. Evidence must earn the right to reject it.
Channel-market fit asks whether a channel's targeting, control, input, output, time, and economics match the product and ICP.

A Type II error is a false negative: a real improvement exists and the test misses it, so something that worked gets abandoned. Alpha controls the false-positive rate; sample size is what protects against false negatives.
Target-customer commitments expose real trade-offs and therefore dominate passive or hypothetical signals.
ICE is disciplined only when its three judgments are explicit and anchored to the constraint and available evidence.
Cohort-by-age views compare like with like and reveal whether new groups hold value better or worse.
Outbound becomes controllable when inputs, stages, qualification, follow-up, and decisions are explicit—not when volume alone increases.
A well-formed metric contains an event, time window, cohort, and denominator. The percentage of a named cohort within a bounded window supplies all four.

Pricing is an engineered structure, not a number. Each structure makes a different promise about how revenue grows as the customer succeeds: per-seat grows with the team, flat rate does not, and identical revenue today can carry completely different futures.
The commitment spectrum gets stronger as the prospect gives up something real—money, time, reputation, or access. A pre-order dominates praise, likes, and opens.

The team lacks the bridge from evidence to prioritisation, execution, and decisions. More activity compounds the disorder.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Explains Sales integration and payback accurately in the learner's own words; the exact term is optional when the idea is clear.

rubric.label: Decision use
rubric.description: Explains when the idea should change a decision, consistently with this course move: Define each handoff's criteria, context, owner and response time, and choose channels by how fast they repay acquisition cost rather than by CAC alone.

key.explanation: Revenue crosses several team handoffs, and each needs an entry criterion, an owner, the context that must travel with it and a response-time SLA; payback measures how long acquisition cash stays tied up before gross profit returns it.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Explains Pre-sales commitment and evidence strength accurately in the learner's own words; the exact term is optional when the idea is clear.

rubric.label: Decision use
rubric.description: Explains when the idea should change a decision, consistently with this course move: Weight every demand signal by what it cost the prospect to give, and require a real commitment before treating demand as proven.

key.explanation: Demand signals sit on a commitment spectrum: social engagement is the easiest to produce and the least meaningful, while a payment or signed commitment is a different category of evidence altogether.
